\subsection{Is the tilt reader valid on generated frames?}
\label{sec:h03-reader-validity}

The generator result rests on one tilt reader.  To test it, 150 frames were drawn from four
generated sources (ANWM, LingBot-World in NF4 and bf16, SolarWM) and 60 controls whose camera
attitude is known exactly (30 simulated pinhole frames from the labelled simulator; 30 TII
fisheye frames through mocap and the recorded mount).  Each frame was read by the reader, by
an independent learned estimator (Perspective Fields) and by a non-learned horizon and
vanishing-point estimator.
The comparison is on \emph{roll}, the image-plane azimuth of world-up, which is invariant to
focal length for a pinhole camera and for any centred radial fisheye model, so it is the one
component of the gravity estimate that can be compared across estimators and camera models on
generated frames.

\label{tab:h03-reader-validity}

Three results follow.  First, the reader's roll error where truth exists is small, 0.6$^\circ$
on simulated and 1.3$^\circ$ on real frames, and it agrees with the independent learned
estimator to 0.7--2.2$^\circ$ on generated frames.  Second, the non-learned estimator cannot
adjudicate: it disagrees with Perspective Fields by 3.2--10.6$^\circ$ on the generated sources
and reads SolarWM's commanded $+20^\circ$ ramp with the opposite sign, so the literal
pre-registered rule (every estimator must agree) fails while the attribution points away from
the reader.  Third, the one unresolved eye-versus-reader case is resolved in the reader's
favour: on LingBot's full-precision level, $+20$ and $-20$ probes the reader holds a constant
roll of $-1.0$ to $-1.2^\circ$ (depicted tilt $3.2$--$4.9^\circ$, no ramp response),
Perspective Fields a constant $-1.3$ to $-3.6^\circ$, and the non-learned sky-line a constant
$+8$ to $+10^\circ$ that is also $+14.8^\circ$ on the \emph{level} clip; the overlays show a
level skyline crossed by an oblique sun-glare edge on the water.  The frames do not roll, and
the generator result does not rest on a reader artefact.

\paragraph{What this does not settle.}
The rule's verdict is ``not valid on generated frames'', and that verdict stands as
pre-registered; the attribution above is an interpretation, not a re-registration.  The
reader's \emph{tilt} (as opposed to roll) error on generated frames is not measured, because
tilt needs the focal length and no generated clip has a truth-bearing control other than the
commanded ramps whose fidelity is the question.  Two learned estimators can share a failure
mode on painterly imagery, and the third, non-learned estimator was meant to catch that and
could not.
